Article Title: FPCE writes to PM Modi, lists 5 key changes to RERA to strengthen homebuyer protection
Article Text:
FPCE writes to PM calling for separating promotion and development of the real estate sector.

The organisation has made five key recommendations:

Separate real estate development from homebuyer protection: Keep the promotion and development of the real estate sector separate from the law designed to protect homebuyers. Re-enact RERA: Bring in a dedicated Real Estate Homebuyer Protection Act that places the interests of homebuyers at its centre. Shift administration to a consumer protection ministry: Entrust the law's administration to a ministry whose primary mandate is consumer protection, such as the Department of Consumer Affairs. Ensure accountability: Introduce an effective accountability framework for real estate regulatory authorities . Prepare a time-bound action plan: Direct the ministry of housing and urban affairs to examine FPCE's report and draw up an action plan with clear timelines.

NEW DELHI: The Forum for People's Collective Efforts (FPCE), which spearheaded the movement for the Real Estate (Regulation and Development) Act, has written to Prime Minister Narendra Modi seeking changes to the law to strengthen homebuyer protection.In its letter, FPCE has called for separating the promotion and development of the real estate sector from the legal framework meant to protect homebuyers.It has also sought the re-enactment of RERA as a dedicated Real Estate Homebuyer Protection Act, with consumer protection at its core.
Article Summary: The Forum for People's Collective Efforts (FPCE) has written to Prime Minister Narendra Modi. It has called for separating the promotion and development of the real estate sector from the legal framework meant to protect homebuyers. The group has also sought the re-enactment of RERA as a dedicated Real Estate Homebuyer Protection Act.

NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Monday permitted the use of green firecrackers in Delhi-NCR on November 7 and 8, between 6 am and 7 am, and 8 pm and 10 pm.The top court said the complete ban on firecrackers would come into effect from November 9.The bench of MM Sundresh and Prasanna B Varale also reiterated that use of firecrackers with Barium and those not approved by CSIR-NEERI as green crackers shall not be permitted.The top court also directed that no firecrackers shall be burst within a 300-metre radius of hospitals, nursing homes, primary and district health centres, old-age homes and notified silence zones."These areas, along with educational institutions, will be declared ‘No-Cracker Zones’ and appropriately marked and publicised," the top court said.The Supreme Court was hearing two petitions, including a suo motu case on air pollution in the National Capital Region covering firecrackers, stubble burning and solid waste management. The other petition seeks a ban on the manufacture of firecrackers.
Article Summary: The top court said the complete ban on firecrackers would come into effect from November 9. The Supreme Court was hearing two petitions, including a suo motu case on air pollution in the National Capital Region. The other petition seeks a ban on the manufacture of firecracker.

Article Title: Sonia Gandhi meets Lalu Yadav in Delhi; Tejashwi shares photos, reminisces UPA-era tie
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Former Congress president Sonia Gandhi met RJD patriarch Lalu Prasad Yadav at the residence of his daughter, Misa Bharti, in New Delhi on Monday and enquired about his health as he continues to undergo treatment at AIIMS in the national capital.Lalu Prasad was recently brought to Delhi for specialised medical consultations after receiving treatment and remaining under observation at the Indira Gandhi Institute of Medical Sciences (IGIMS) in Patna.His condition is currently stable, according to family members.Tejashwi Yadav , on social media platform X, recalled the political association between Sonia Gandhi and his father during the UPA government (2004-2014).He highlighted welfare initiatives undertaken during that period for farmers, young people, soldiers and the common public, as well as key legislations such as MGNREGA, the Right to Education (RTE) Act and the Right to Information (RTI) Act.He also pointed out that the then Prime Minister Manmohan Singh 's government had allocated more than Rs 1.45 lakh crore for Bihar's development.The Bihar leader of the opposition said Sonia Gandhi, whose memoir, "Belonging: A Journey of Love", is scheduled for release on November 10, had personally expressed a desire to meet his father after learning that he was in Delhi for a medical check-up."Lalu Prasad had come to Delhi for his routine medical check-up. I also met Sonia Gandhi and informed her about this. She herself expressed a desire to meet Lalu Prasad, which is why she visited him today. Lalu Prasad and Sonia Gandhi have shared a good relationship from the very beginning. They have stood by and supported each other during difficult circumstances. Our family and the Gandhi family have also shared a longstanding relationship. The purpose of today's meeting was to enquire about Lalu Prasad's health. They had not met for a long time, which is why they met today," Tejashwi wrote on X in Hindi.Lalu Yadav also posted about this meet with Sonia Gandhi on X, writing: "It was recalled how, during the days of the UPA government, we implemented transparent and public welfare schemes for the youth, farmers, soldiers, and the common man, and how the countrymen were empowered through laws like MGNREGA, RTE, and RTI. Under the leadership of Sardar Manmohan Singh ji, how we provided more than 1 lakh 45 thousand crore rupees for the development of Bihar. "Tejashwi also spoke about the INDIA bloc's rally at Delhi's Ramlila Maidan, saying opposition parties would need to remain united to take on the challenges facing the country.He said the gathering was not the end of the campaign against Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar and insisted that the opposition would continue pressing for action against him."We will not win this battle unless we stand united. We did gather yesterday, but that was not the final event. We are not the kind of people who will sit quietly until action is taken against Gyanesh Kumar," he said.The RJD leader also hit back at the BJP for describing the opposition rally as a failure. Questioning the ruling party's reaction, he alleged that the rally had unsettled the BJP."Why are they so nervous? If the rally had been a flop, why would there be any need to prove it was a flop? They know that there is unease and turmoil. They are troubled and disappointed because their theft has been exposed," he said.

Article Title: 'Don't travel by air. Next case': SC judge on plea alleging 700% airfare hike
Article Text:
The court did not take up the plea at that stage and proceeded to the next matter.

NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Monday responded sharply to a plea highlighting a steep surge in airfares, with Justice Vikram Nath telling the counsel, “Don’t travel by air. Next case,” before moving on to the next matter.The exchange took place when the counsel mentioned the plea before the court, claiming that airfares had increased by as much as 700 per cent. Arguing that air travel was an essential service, the counsel said the steep rise in ticket prices amounted to a violation of Article 14 of the Constitution, which guarantees equality before the law.“The airfares have increased to 700%. It is an essential service. Violation of Article 14,” the counsel submitted, according to Live Law.Justice Nath responded, “Don’t travel by air. Next case.”The court did not take up the plea at that stage and proceeded to the next matter. No order was passed on the submission.Meanwhile, India has adopted new airfare rules where government will not interfere in the process except “in an extraordinary situation (where) it considers it necessary to do so in the public interest.” Notified under the Bharatiya Vayuyan Niyam, 2026, which will be applicable from Jan 1, 2027, government has continued its policy of letting market forces determine airfares without government interference.TOI reported on Oct 17 that India has no plans to regulate or cap airfares in the free market under which airlines here operate under the new airfare policy being finalised. However, it will keep a “strong lever” on airlines to ensure they don’t resort to very sharp surges in “exceptional and extraordinary circumstances” that see demand rising for certain routes.
Article Summary: The exchange took place when the counsel mentioned the plea before the court. Arguing that air travel was an essential service, the counsel said the steep rise in ticket prices amounted to a violation of Article 14 of the Constitution. The court did not take up the plea at that stage and proceeded to the next matter.

Article Title: ‘Rahul Gandhi fostering chaos’: BJP questions Congress over SIR row
Article Text:
Sudhanshu targets Rahul Gandhi over SIR row

NEW DELHI: BJP MP Sudhanshu Trivedi on Monday accused the Congress and Lok Sabha LoP Rahul Gandhi of spreading a “false narrative” over the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, alleging that the Opposition was attempting to create confusion and undermine constitutional institutions.Calling Rahul Gandhi the “greatest challenge to India’s democracy”, Trivedi claimed that certain forces, both within and outside the country, were unhappy with India's progress in areas such as artificial intelligence, defence production and national security, and that the Opposition had become a “mere plaything in their hands”.Trivedi also questioned the Congress's allegations over the electoral roll revision process, pointing to the role of Booth Level Officers (BLOs) and Booth Level Agents (BLAs). He said the Election Commission had appointed around 12 lakh BLOs across the country, while political parties had appointed approximately 22 lakh BLAs to monitor the process of adding and deleting names from electoral rolls“Were the Congress Party’s BLAs asleep or under the influence of intoxicants? They signed off on these lists or, if they didn’t sign, did they raise any objections?” he asked.The BJP leader argued that political parties had representatives to monitor the revision process and questioned why the Congress was raising objections if its agents had not flagged discrepancies at the time.Trivedi also cited the Congress's electoral performance in several states to counter Rahul Gandhi's claims about anti-incumbency and the party's prospects. He said the Congress had not had a chief minister in Odisha for 25 years, had been out of power in Gujarat since 1995, and in Uttar Pradesh and Bihar since 1990.“These states account for 120 seats,” he said, adding that the Congress had struggled to win even 10 seats across states with a combined 230 Lok Sabha constituencies. He questioned how the party expected to reach the 272-seat majority mark under these circumstances.Trivedi further referred to Kerala, where the Congress's political opponents are in power, and cited state leader Ramesh Chennithala's reported remarks that they had benefited from the SIR exercise. He used this to question the Opposition's criticism of the revision process.His remarks come amid the Opposition's intensified campaign against the SIR exercise. On Sunday, November 1, INDIA bloc leaders, including Rahul Gandhi, Mallikarjun Kharge, Priyanka Gandhi Vadra, Mamata Banerjee, Akhilesh Yadav, Tejashwi Yadav and Farooq Abdullah, held a mega rally at Delhi's Ramlila Maidan under the banner of 'Vote Bachao, Desh Bachao'.The rally followed a march from Minto Road towards the venue, with Opposition leaders accusing the Election Commission of large-scale voter deletions and demanding the resignation of chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.In another X post, Union home minister Amit Shah also targetted Congress."Facing repeated rejections in elections, Congress is now hell-bent on grabbing power by destroying democracy through anarchy. Citizens have braced themselves to shield our democracy from these attacks. This evening, will join the Save Democracy, Remove Anarchy march in Hyderabad," he wrote .
Article Summary: BJP MP Sudhanshu Trivedi accuses Rahul Gandhi of spreading a ‘false narrative’ over the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. He claims the Opposition was attempting to create confusion and undermine constitutional institutions.

Article Title: Ayodhya Ram temple donation embezzlement case: Chargesheet filed, Supreme Court allows petitioners to assist trial
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Uttar Pradesh government on Monday informed the Supreme Court that a chargesheet has been filed in the alleged embezzlement of donations at the Shri Ram Janmabhoomi temple in Ayodhya, with the court permitting the petitioners to assist the local magistrate during the trial.A bench led by Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant disposed of the petitions concerning the alleged theft of temple donations and directed the judicial magistrate to proceed with the case in accordance with the law.The Supreme Court also clarified that it had not expressed any opinion on the merits of the allegations.Solicitor General Tushar Mehta, appearing for the Uttar Pradesh government, informed the court that the alleged theft took place during the counting of donations at the temple. He said certain officials involved in counting the money would allegedly take the funds and either invest them elsewhere or deposit them into bank accounts.Taking note of the public interest involved in the matter, the court permitted the writ petitioners to assist the magistrate in the proceedings in the same manner as victims are allowed to assist criminal proceedings.The court clarified that its decision to allow the petitioners to participate in the trial should not be construed as an observation on the merits of the case.The proceedings will now continue before the local magistrate, who will examine the allegations in accordance with the law.
Article Summary: Supreme Court allows petitioners to assist the local magistrate during the trial. Chargesheet has been filed in the alleged embezzlement of donations at the Shri Ram Janmabhoomi temple in Ayodhya. Solicitor General Tushar Mehta, appearing for the Uttar Pradesh government, informed the court that the alleged theft took place during the counting of donations.

Article Title: INDIA bloc rally at Ramlila Maidan saw creative expression take centre stage as slogans, posters and placards delivered the message
Article Text:
Ramlila Maidan became the space for INDIA bloc members to make their presence felt

NEW DELHI: If the stage at Ramlila Maidan sent out a strong message of a united opposition that will not relent till it sees Gyanesh Kumar's removed as Chief Election Commissioner, the atmosphere at the packed grounds reflected the same sense of coming together as flags of all hues representing the diverse ideologies of INDIA parties were held up by workers and supporters.From slogans like "Vote Chor Gaddi Chhod" to the euphoric response of the crowd to repeated chanting of "Inquilab Zindabad" - the Ramlila Maidan on Sunday became the space for INDIA bloc members to make their presence felt. The RJD and Samajwadi Party flags shared space with a sea of flags representing the Left parties - a reflection of how diverse ideologies and ideas converged on ground for a common cause.Congress leader Rahul Gandhi got the loudest applause from the crowd that had been growing strong since 9 in the morning and remained eager to stay even as the main speeches only took off at 3 pm as the top leaders of the INDIA parties arrived on stage after the Vote Bachao, Desh Bachao March from CP Minto Road Junction to the rally venue.With 2027 set to see crucial assembly polls in UP, Punjab and Uttarakhand, one saw Samajwadi Party supporters assert their presence as they rooted for party supremo Akhilesh Yadav cheering loudly and waving the Party flag. Yadav delivered a fiery speech shooting sharply at Modi saying, "Jo UP sey aayey they woh UP sey hi jayengey". He also raised the issue of "chanda chori" from Ram Temple Trust in Ayodhya.Reflecting on the INDIA campaign so far, CPI(ML) Liberation general secretary Dipankar Bhattacharya was the first speaker who set the set the tone by highlighting how the parties in the Alliance have unitedly taken up and build the outreach on the issue of SIR and working of Election Commission under CEC Gyanesh Kumar."We took the decision to hit the streets on Sept 30 at the INDIA bloc meeting and since then the slogan of "vote chor gaddi chhod" and "vote bachao, desh bachao" has resonated across the country. Since they started SIR in Bihar people have suffered and faced its impact and to counter it and the autocratic working of the Central govt, the people have responded with this "jan sailaab" he highlighted. Bhattacharya and CPI(M) general secretary MA Baby referred to the ongoing protests as nothing short of a second freedom struggle.RJD's Tejashwi Yadav chose to draw from the epic Mahabharat to make his point. "Vote chori key liyey Mahabharat ka ayojan kiya Hai Ramlila Maidan mein..," he said in Hindi. He cited the example of Shakuni and his dice to highlight that there was a lack of a level-playing field there and alleged that the same situation existed in the Modi regime with Gyanesh Kumar as CEC. He demanded that Gyanesh Kumar should be tried for treason. Rahul Gandhi had raised this at the public impeachment on Saturday and reiterated the same on Sunday.Interestingly, TMC chairperson and former West Bengal CM Mamata Banerjee while delivering a fiery attack on CEC Gyanesh Kumar, was the only speaker who after highlighting the unity in the INDIA bloc, lauded and backed the efforts of the Cockroach Janta Party and Gen Z in taking up issues ranging from concerns in the examination system to SIR and EC related protests.It was interesting to see a large presence of youth with student outfits. The Left linked student wings like AISA, SFI, AISF and Krantkari Yuva Sangathan joined with full fervour alongside the NSUI. One one side there were the Left students groups who chose to break into an impromtu performance amid the crowd as all waited for the INDIA leaders to arrive. Then one saw a large group of ethnically dressed women and men from Jharkhand play their traditional instruments.An RJD supporter was busy singing patriotic songs, and then there was a stir as one man arrived drenched in sculpted clay depicting Mahatma Gandhi holding the Constitution. There were others too holding cutouts and impressions from the Constitution.Posters calling for Gyanesh Kumar's ouster in Gen Z lingo - "It's done Bro!" and a young man holding up a cutout of BR Ambedkar which read "Ab toh Ungli Uthegi" to a group of men who came wearing a garland of plastic fingers with red stains to symbolise the loss of the voting rights - the rally saw people convey the political message on the importance of voting rights with creative zeal.
Article Summary: The Ramlila Maidan on Sunday became the space for INDIA bloc members to make their presence felt. The RJD and Samajwadi Party flags shared space with a sea of flags representing the Left parties - a reflection of how diverse ideologies and ideas converged on ground for a common cause.

Article Title: J&K: NC Srinagar MP Mehdi to quit party tomorrow to fight it back on 'ideological' turf
Article Text:
Article 370, Waqf, BJP: Mehdi explains why he is quitting NC and challenging its ideology

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

BUDGAM: At the entrance of the National Conference (NC) Srinagar MP Aga Ruhullah Mehdi home’s two large banners at the gate sum up the message he wants to convey. One reads, “Wada kursi se bada hai” (a promise is bigger than a chair), while the other says, “Kirdar ki siyasat, usoolon ki siyasat” (politics of character, politics of principles).Inside the hall, party workers gathered in small groups, discussing the fallout of Mehdi's announcement that he would formally resign from as NC MP at a rally here on November 3 on the death anniversary of his father. One worker said, “even at a barber's shop, people do not give up their chairs for someone else even if that person is older. Here is a man willing to leave his chair for the sake of principles. Who gives up a chair like that. ”Inside in his room, sitting calmly in his chair, Mehdi insists his decision to part ways with the party is final and there is no going back.“I have been part of this NC for 24 years. I joined it believing that it stood for autonomy and the rights of the people of J&K. But after the abrogation of Article 370 , whatever remnants of autonomy we had were taken away and the party despite getting a strong mandate in the 2024 Assembly elections on the promise of challenging the status quo, failed to honour it,” Mehdi told the TOI, accusing the chief minister Omar Abdullah of diluting his electoral position on Article 370, Waqf Amendment Act, Muslim issues, reservations and moving closer to the BJP, “to the point of submission.”In the room, hanging on the wall was a large photograph of his father, Aga Syed Mehdi, a prominent Shia cleric and Congress leader who was assassinated in a terrorist attack on November 3, 2000.“I understand it will be long fight but I am not afraid," he said, hastily added that whenever the NC faced an ideological challenge, it found it tough to defend its position. The People’s Democratic Party (PDP) managed, he said, for a brief period, to offer it such a challenge before joining an alliance with the BJP in 2015 reduced party to three members today. “There was also an ideological contest between the NC and the Hurriyat Conference in Jammu and Kashmir for many years. I am not endorsing the Hurriyat Conference as it represented the other extreme. But when it came to ideological contestation, the streets were dominated by the other side, not the National Conference,” he said.He said people need to replace traditional political forces like NC and PDP and other like them with more potent one having conviction. “The common problem with these two political parties and others like them, is their lack of character. It is what they have in common. People trusted the NC and the PDP. But they delivered the same kind of results,” he added.Mehdi, who has been critical of the CM and his government, said the chief minister normalised the post-abrogation arrangement through his government, Assembly and other constitutional institutions. “The party began speaking the very language that the BJP wanted people across the country to speak after the abrogation of Article 370,” he said. He said he found further clarity after NC president Farooq Abdullah recently said in an interview that if Mehdi believed what he says he was free to resign from the party.“Referring to me Dr Abdullah said that if I believed Article 370 could be restored, I was free to move out and get it restored. Effectively, he was saying that he himself did not believe Article 370 could not be restored. This again raises the question, if he does not believe it can be restored constitutionally, why people of Jammu and Kashmir were given the assurance during the poll campaign. In the same interview, he asked me to resign from the party as, in his view, I had become an irritant in the process of normalising the post-abrogation status quo. They wanted me to leave the party because I am questioning their position,” he added.Mehdi also rejected the claim that the NC alone was responsible for his victory in the 2024 Lok Sabha elections from Srinagar. “The NC never crossed 1.5 lakh votes in this parliamentary constituency in 30 to 40 years. This time I got nearly 3.80 lakh votes. The bulk of the support came from people in South Kashmir who were not associated with the NC,” he said as number of areas of South Kashmir’s Pulwama and Shopian were added to Srinagar in the delimitation exercise of 2023. He, however, said that he contested on the NC ticket and used the party's name and symbol, making his resignation necessary as he sought to distance himself from the organisation.Mehdi, who is also a prominent shia leader, said he was reaching out to people from different walks of life, including journalists, lawyers, doctors and teachers, to build a credible political alternative.“I am looking for people with no baggage, who have conviction and are willing to walk this path,” he said, adding that the structure and name of any new organisation would be decided later.He said he might contest future by-elections from Srinagar constituency as an independent candidate but insisted his decision to resign was not driven by electoral ambition. “I am not bargaining with people over what I will get in return for resigning. This has nothing to do with electoral results or how people behave. It is a call of conscience and a matter of principles,” he said.
Article Summary: National Conference (NC) Srinagar MP Aga Ruhullah Mehdi resigns from party. Mehdi accuses Omar Abdullah of diluting his electoral position on Article 370, Waqf Amendment Act, Muslim issues, reservations and moving closer to the BJP.

Two Congress workers were arrested on Monday for allegedly throwing beer bottles at the BJP's Kerala state headquarters, Mararji Bhavan, in Thiruvananthapuram around a month ago, police said.The arrested individuals have been identified as Sujith Kumar and Arun, both associated with local Congress units, according to the news agency PTI.According to police, the incident occurred amid heightened tensions between rival political groups following a series of clashes involving different political outfits in Thiruvananthapuram district.The situation had worsened after Youth Congress workers waved black flags at the convoy of Union Home Minister Amit Shah during the last week of September. Article Title: Fake claims, evasion of Rs 5.3 crore land, techie couple in I-T net
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: In a stern message to those making false income tax claims, authorities have carried out a rare search action on an IT professional and his wife, estimating alleged bogus claims and tax evasion of Rs 5.3 crore over five years, according to the department. The couple also face charges of forging documents.Tax officials found that deduction claims involved fake political donations, interest on home and education loans, while rental income was not disclosed. They had purchased half-a-dozen properties using some of these funds.It all started with the wife's tax return claiming a deduction of over Rs 40 lakh for a donation to a political party. While her Form 16 showed deductions of around Rs 1.2 lakh, the return claimed an additional deduction. When the claim was verified with the party, officials found that the taxpayer had actually donated Rs 50, for which a receipt had been issued. Investigators found that the receipt had been digitally modified and several fabricated receipts generated to support the claim of a donation exceeding Rs 40 lakh.But the couple, who live in Delhi-NCR, did not give in easily. When summoned during the investigation, the husband, who filed the returns, not only presented the "modified" receipts but also submitted bank statements to support the claim.Officials sought to verify the statements with the bank, as the transactions did not tally.Loan payments, credit card payments and bank transfers, including transfers to their own account, had been forged to show them as political donations.The couple had claimed nearly Rs 3 crore in education loan interest for studies at Yale University. An interest certificate was submitted. During probe, officials discovered that no family member of the couple under scrutiny had ever studied at Yale and that the certificate had been prepared using ChatGPT.The couple also made a bogus housing loan claim, with both spouses describing themselves as the sole owner of the same property, although they have now admitted that it was jointly owned. Contrary to their claims, the property was always rented out and was not self-occupied.In their returns, one spouse had claimed nil rental income and interest payment of Rs 2 lakh, while the other had claimed up to Rs 5 lakh as interest income. Since tax returns now require individuals to disclose loan account number and the bank, the name of the bank was changed in one case and the loan amount increased to Rs 6 crore, with interest claimed at Rs 8 lakh. The probe revealed that the loan had been repaid in 2015, while the claims under scrutiny related to the period beginning FY2021-22. The property was earning rent of Rs 10-16 lakh during this period.Dealing with the couple has not been easy. When their case was first picked up, the husband shifted the deduction claim for political donations under Section 80GGC to donations to charities under Section 80G, without surrendering the claim.The couple now face penalties and other legal action.
Article Summary: IT professional and wife face Rs 5.3 crore taxevasion allegations over fabricated donation and loan claims, including forged documents and receipts. Article Title: Introspect on need to improve judiciary responsiveness: CJI
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Flagging the importance of timely intervention by courts in crucial matters, CJI Surya Kant said the difference between justice and injustice was not in the final judgement but in whether the court intervened when "intervention was most needed".He underlined the need for the judiciary, particularly constitutional courts, to introspect to further improve their working and to make listing of cases "more transparent and predictable".Speaking at the platinum jubilee celebration of Kerala HC, CJI Kant said constitutional justice in India did not begin and end in New Delhi and its strength lay in the robust network of 25 HCs spread across the country, each entrusted with the duty of protecting rights and upholding the rule of law.He said HCs were better placed to deal with citizens' problems as they were closely connected with the everyday realities of people."It is in this context that I wish to emphasise the extraordinary constitutional significance of Article 226. Its breadth is one of the greatest strengths of our judicial architecture. While Article 32 guarantees access to SC for enforcement of fundamental rights, Article 226 empowers HCs to issue appropriate writs and directions not only for fundamental rights but also for other legal rights.This wide constitutional canvas allows HCs to fashion meaningful remedies across diverse legal, statutory, administrative and contractual disputes. Equally important is their power to grant timely interim protection," the CJI said.He said there has been a growing tendency of litigants to approach SC requesting directions for urgent listing or early hearing of matters pending before HCs and asked whether the present process could be improved, including listing of cases."SC has consistently respected the institutional autonomy of HCs, including their authority to regulate their own rosters. That position is rooted in respect for the constitutional status of these institutions. Yet, the frequency of such requests invites us to consider whether there is room to improve the responsiveness of our processes. We must ask ourselves: Can urgent matters be identified more effectively? Can listing procedures be made more transparent and predictable? Can technology assist in prioritising cases where delay may cause irreversible prejudice?. .." he said."These are not questions of institutional criticism but of collective responsibility," the CJI added.
Article Summary: CJI Surya Kant calls for more transparent and predictable case listings. He says timely court intervention can make the difference between justice and injustice. He underlined the need for the judiciary, particularly constitutional courts, to introspect to further improve their working.

NEW DELHI: India has adopted new airfare rules where government will not interfere in the process except “in an extraordinary situation (where) it considers it necessary to do so in the public interest. ” Notified under the Bharatiya Vayuyan Niyam, 2026, which will be applicable from Jan 1, 2027, government has continued its policy of letting market forces determine airfares without government interference.TOI reported on Oct 17 that India has no plans to regulate or cap airfares in the free market under which airlines here operate under the new airfare policy being finalised. Article Title: Golden Triangle's North East drug trade thrives on barter
Article Text:
Cash doesn't cross Myanmar border, payments made in kind: ED

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: International illicit drug syndicates operating out of the Golden Triangle of Myanmar, Thailand and Laos have turned to age-old barter trade, under which drugs like heroin and methamphetamine are smuggled into India through the porous borders of Northeastern states and payments are made in kind through supplies of petrol, diesel, flour, edible oil, groceries, medicines, footwear and clothing from their Indian network.Drug lords across border ensure transactions are made without any money actually crossing border, according to an investigation report compiled by the ED after week-long searches at 38 locations across the Northeast last week.Myanmar has already replaced Afghanistan as world's largest illicit opium-producing region. With precursor chemicals moved from India to Myanmar, where drug manufacturing units are located, finished heroin, brown sugar and synthetic drug methamphetamine tablets are produced and carried across the Tiau river at Zokhawthar, the border crossing opposite Khawmawi in Myanmar. Consignments are staged at Champhai, from where they travel down the Champhai-Aizawl road and NH-06A to Aizawl, Vairengte and then to Assam and the rest of India, the ED report said.ED has traced intermediaries who procured and supplied goods to syndicates in Myanmar. Over 1,400 mule bank accounts, mostly belonging to traders who procured these goods and supplied them to the network, have been frozen. Transactions involving goods worth over Rs 270 crore have been identified so far and six persons arrested.These transactions were handled by illicit money exchangers, or hawala networks, in Champhai, including Rs 125 crore in cash received from Assam, Nagaland, WB, Tripura & Delhi, ED said.Significantly, drug money reaching hawala accounts in Aizawl and Champhai came substantially from Delhi, Kolkata and Mumbai, ED added. Illegal money is converted into ordinary, commercially marketable goods, which are sent to border towns of Mizoram and onward to Myanmar."The banking system is thus used only for Indian leg of the transaction, where the payment looks like an ordinary trade payment backed by a GST invoice. The cross-border leg moves as goods and leaves no money trail. In effect, fuel, flour and groceries have become currency in which Myanmar-based drug suppliers are paid," ED said.The probe is in progress to identify consignees in border towns, those who move goods across border, Myanmar-based recipients, petrol pumps, shops and suppliers paid in the same manner, and money exchangers directing the accounts. ED is also tracing and attaching further proceeds of crime as it works to dismantle the financial networks sustaining narcotics trafficking.
Article Summary: Myanmar has already replaced Afghanistan as world's largest illicit opium- producing region. With precursor chemicals moved from India to Myanmar, finished heroin, brown sugar and synthetic drug methamphetamine tablets are produced. Transactions involving goods worth over Rs 270 crore have been identified so far and six persons arrested.

For many Indians, the day begins with a cup of milky chai, followed by breakfast cooked in ghee. Lunch may come with a bowl of curd and paneer on the menu, while a Sunday meal is often incomplete without chicken curry.These familiar food habits are so deeply woven into everyday life that giving up all animal-derived products can seem like a difficult choice.But for people who turn vegan, the change goes beyond replacing meat with vegetables. It means rethinking everyday ingredients, from milk and butter to honey, as well as choices involving clothing, cosmetics and other products.“There are alternatives for practically everything. You can make curd at home using plant milk, use tofu instead of paneer, and use different nut and soy milks,” says Sarahana, who has been vegan since 2018.On World Vegan Day, observed on November 1, the question is not just why people choose veganism, but what it takes to follow the lifestyle.According to The Vegan Society, veganism is a way of living that seeks to exclude, as far as possible and practicable, all forms of animal exploitation and cruelty.While a vegan diet avoids meat, fish, eggs, dairy and honey, the lifestyle also extends to products made from animals, those tested on animals and activities that use animals for entertainment.For some, the decision is rooted in animal welfare; for others, environmental concerns or health considerations play a role.But the experiences of vegans show that the transition is as much about changing everyday habits as it is about changing one's perspective.India has a long tradition of vegetarian food, but veganism goes a step further by excluding all animal-derived products, including milk, curd, ghee, paneer and honey.According to estimates compiled by World Population Review, around 9% of India's population followed a vegan diet in 2021, amounting to an estimated 121.5 million people. The country also has a substantial vegetarian population, reflecting its diverse food traditions.However, the figure should be treated as an estimate rather than a definitive count, as veganism surveys often rely on self-reported responses and vary in methodologies.A vegan diet does not necessarily mean giving up familiar Indian food or relying on expensive, imported alternatives. Dal, rice, roti, rajma, chole, idli, dosa, poha, upma and vegetable dishes can all be part of a vegan diet, provided they are prepared without animal-derived ingredients.Utkarsh Garg, a representative of People for the Ethical Treatment of Animals (PETA), says their meals are a mix of familiar Indian dishes and plant-based alternatives.“Breakfast is usually a protein smoothie bowl or soaked oats, although I’m definitely not above a plate of poha, chhole-kulche or one enormous aloo paratha when the mood strikes!”“Lunch and dinner usually include things like tofu, soybeans, dals, rajma and plenty of vegetables. My current obsession is tempeh. I seem to be finding increasingly creative excuses to put it into everything I eat.”“As for living without milk, paneer, curd or ghee, I genuinely don’t find it difficult anymore. There are so many vegan alternatives available now, and many things are surprisingly easy and inexpensive to make at home as well.” Utkarsh said.Sarahana says she relies largely on everyday Indian food rather than packaged substitutes.“As for food, my everyday diet is actually quite simple and Indian. Dal, rice, roti, vegetables, chickpeas, rajma, seasonal produce and different legumes. There are so many naturally plant-based foods available in India. You don’t need expensive imported alternatives or packaged vegan products to survive without dairy.“There are alternatives for practically everything. You can make curd at home using plant milk, use tofu instead of paneer, and use different nut and soy milks. Ghee is essentially clarified butter, and personally, I don’t feel the need to replace it.”The distinction is important. A vegan diet does not require a direct substitute for every non-vegan food. It can instead be built around naturally plant-based ingredients that are already widely used in Indian kitchens.For Utkarsh, the decision began in childhood. Watching a chicken being slaughtered made them connect the food on their plate with the animal it came from. He turned vegetarian that day and later went vegan.“For me, veganism has always been about animals. I’ve loved animals for as long as I can remember. While most kids my age were watching Cartoon Network or Pogo, I was glued to National Geographic, completely fascinated by dogs, cats, cows, snakes, and pretty much every animal I came across,” Utkarsh said.As he learnt more about animal exploitation, vegetarianism no longer felt enough. “My love for animals naturally led me to veganism. I’ve been vegan for four years now, and honestly, it is one of the best decisions I have ever made. More than changing what I eat or wear, it has changed the way I look at the world and my place in it.”For Sarahana, the turning point came in 2018, when she watched a video of a pregnant cow being slaughtered after she was no longer productive for the dairy industry.“My decision came from questioning something very basic: why do we, as human beings, consider ourselves superior to other animals? Why do we love some animals, consider some family, see some as entertainment, and others as food?” she said.While studying gender, Sarahana began drawing parallels between the exploitation of women's bodies and that of female animals in the dairy industry.“How can I study feminism, gender and the exploitation of female bodies and not extend that understanding beyond human beings? How can I talk about patriarchy and exploitation while continuing to pay an industry that repeatedly impregnates female animals, takes away their babies and exploits their reproductive systems?” she said.Coming from a Dalit community, Sarahana also views veganism through the lens of social justice, questioning how societies decide whose lives are valued.“We love cats and dogs, welcome them into our homes and call them family, but we look at chickens, goats and buffaloes and see food. We have created categories of animals that deserve affection and animals that can be exploited,” she added.One common perception is that veganism is an expensive lifestyle, largely because plant-based milk, meat substitutes and other packaged alternatives can cost more than conventional products. However, both Utkarsh and Sarahana say that a vegan diet need not depend on these products.Utkarsh points out that many Indian staples are naturally plant-based. “India is one of the easiest places in which to eat vegan, because so much of the food we already know and love either naturally contains no animal-derived ingredients or can be veganised with ridiculously small changes.“Think about dal, rajma, chole, idli, dosa, poha, upma, roti, sabzis, rice dishes and countless regional foods. Veganism doesn’t have to mean buying an expensive imported mock meat or drinking a fancy packaged plant milk every morning. Those products are great if you enjoy them, but they aren’t what veganism depends on.”Sarahana agrees that the bigger challenge is often social rather than financial.“I don’t think being vegan in India is inherently expensive. Our traditional food already has so many affordable plant-based options. What can become expensive is the packaged vegan alternatives, not the basic diet itself. The bigger challenge is social conditioning. At family gatherings, weddings or even casual conversations, you constantly have to explain why you don’t consume something that everyone else considers normal. ”Both say their families initially had questions and reservations. Utkarsh says their family is now supportive and has started incorporating more vegan foods and products into their lives. Sarahana, meanwhile, says she continues to face comments that she has been “brainwashed”.Veganism is often associated with better health, but a plant-based diet is not automatically a balanced one. Its nutritional value depends on the foods included and whether essential nutrients are adequately supplied.Dt Gausiya Aziz, consultant and head of nutrition and dietetics at SPARSH Hospital, Yelahanka, says a well-planned vegan diet can support cardiovascular and metabolic health.“Research suggests that plant-based dietary patterns rich in fibre, antioxidants and unsaturated fats can help lower LDL cholesterol, improve blood pressure and support healthy weight management. They may also reduce the risk of developing type 2 diabetes,” she says.However, claims that veganism automatically prevents cancer, reverses chronic diseases or guarantees a longer life are exaggerated, she cautions. Health outcomes depend on overall diet quality, lifestyle and individual medical conditions.A key concern is meeting nutritional requirements. Vitamin B12, iron, calcium, vitamin D, iodine, zinc, omega-3 fatty acids and protein need particular attention.Vitamin B12 is especially important because reliable natural plant-based sources are limited. Fortified foods or supplements may therefore be necessary.Aziz recommends a varied diet containing whole grains, legumes, vegetables, fruits, nuts and seeds, along with appropriate supplementation and regular nutritional assessment.Utkarsh says he pay close attention to their nutritional needs and take vitamin B12 supplements.“I am also quite particular about my nutrition. I take my B12 regularly and pay attention to vitamin D and other essential nutrients. B12 supplementation is important for vegans, and these supplements are accessible at pharmacies,” he said.The PETA representative added that he has noticed less bloating since turning vegan and feel healthier, but stresses that dietary planning matters.“Of course, I think any diet needs to be properly planned rather than treated as automatically healthy simply because it carries a particular label. For me, veganism has actually made me more conscious of what I eat and what my body needs.”Aziz also warns that highly processed vegan foods are not necessarily healthy. Packaged snacks, meat substitutes and desserts can contain high amounts of sodium, refined carbohydrates, added sugars and saturated fats. She advises prioritising minimally processed foods and checking nutritional labels.“Children, pregnant women and older adults have specific nutritional requirements that demand careful consideration before adopting a vegan diet. During childhood, adequate energy, protein, calcium, iron, vitamin B12 and vitamin D are essential for growth and development. Pregnant women must additionally ensure sufficient folate, iodine, choline and omega-3 fatty acids to support maternal health and fetal development. Older adults should prioritise protein intake, calcium and vitamin D to preserve muscle strength and bone health. Vitamin B12 supplementation is particularly important across these groups,” Aziz added.Nutritionist Aziz also recommends consulting a qualified dietitian or healthcare professional before making significant dietary changes.Animal welfare is not the only reason people choose veganism. Environmental concerns are also part of the conversation.Aziz says vegan diets generally have a lower environmental footprint than diets containing substantial amounts of animal products, particularly red meat and dairy.Plant-based food production typically requires less agricultural land and generates fewer greenhouse gas emissions than livestock farming. It can also reduce pressure on biodiversity and freshwater resources.However, the environmental impact varies with farming methods, transportation, processing and food waste. Choosing locally available, seasonal and minimally processed plant foods can help reduce the footprint further.For Utkarsh, the values behind veganism are also connected to ideas of compassion and non-violence.“We grow up hearing about ahimsa and vasudhaiva kutumbakam, the idea that the world is one family. To me, animals shouldn’t be excluded from that circle of compassion simply because they belong to another species,” he said.Going vegan involves more than changing what is on the plate. It can mean checking product labels, asking about ingredients when eating out and finding alternatives to everyday items.Some medications and personal-care products may also contain animal-derived ingredients, making it important to check rather than assume that a product is vegan.For someone considering the transition, Utkarsh suggests starting by understanding where everyday products come from.“For anyone considering going vegan because they care about animals, I would say: start by looking. Look honestly at where our milk, meat, eggs, leather, wool, silk, cosmetics and entertainment come from.”“Once I did that, veganism stopped feeling like something I was ‘giving up’. It started feeling like the most natural extension of something I had believed all along.”Sarahana says the idea is to extend compassion beyond the animals people traditionally consider companions or pets.She also points to the growing number of Indian businesses offering vegan alternatives. For her, such businesses are helping make animal-free choices more accessible.For those thinking of making the switch, the practical starting point may be simple: understand what a vegan diet excludes, plan for essential nutrients and explore the plant-based foods already available in the kitchen.World Vegan Day was established in 1994 by Louise Wallis, then president of The Vegan Society, to mark the 50th anniversary of the organisation's founding in November 1944.The day is now observed annually on November 1 to raise awareness about veganism and its ethical, environmental and health-related aspects.
Article Summary: World Vegan Day is observed annually on November 1. India has a long tradition of vegetarian food, but veganism goes a step further by excluding all animal- derived products. Around 9% of India's population followed a vegan diet in 2021, amounting to 121.5 million people.

Article Title: Poverty removal not just slogan: PM Modi on World Bank data
Article Text:
PM Narendra Modi cites World Bank data showing India's extreme poverty rate fell 90% to 2.6% between 2011 and 2023, with nearly 50 crore people lifted out of extreme poverty.

NEW DELHI: India has recorded one of the fastest poverty declines in the world, with the extreme poverty rate in the country "collapsing" by 90% between 2011 and 2023 to a low of 2.6%, Prime Minister Narendra Modi said on Saturday, while asserting that elimination of poverty is a commitment for his govt."A historic fall in poverty. A generational rise in opportunity... Gareebi hatao was never a slogan for us. It is our commitment. From more than 1 in 4 Indians to roughly 1 in 38 (in extreme poverty)," the PM posted on Instagram Saturday, citing the World Bank's latest numbers. He highlighted that nearly 50 crore people had moved out of poverty during these 12 years.Besides, Modi added, employment had grown by 13.4 crore between 2017 and 2023, which was nearly twice the increase in India's working age population. "Inequality has fallen sharply. India's Gini index has dropped by over 20% from 29 in 2011 to 23 in 2023," the Prime Minister said in the Instagram post. The Gini index reflects how equitable is the distribution of income or wealth across a population, with a lower number indicating greater equality.World Bank's latest Poverty and Equity brief, released last week, said that poverty rate in India, defined at $4.2 a day, will decline to 12.1% in 2028 from 57.7% in 2011, having fallen to 16.1% in 2023.Meanwhile, extreme poverty, defined as spending $3 a day, declined from 27.1% in 2011 to 2.6% in 2023."This progress was mainly driven by strong consumption growth; rising employment, especially among women; and expanded social transfers, including food subsidies. As poverty declined, it became increasingly concentrated among households with lower education, fewer assets, limited access to stable employment and higher dependency ratios. Wage disparities, however, remain pronounced, as median earnings among the top 10% of workers were about 13 times those of the bottom 10% in 2023," the World Bank had said.
Article Summary: PM Narendra Modi cites World Bank data showing India's extreme poverty rate fell 90% to 2.6% between 2011 and 2023. He highlighted that nearly 50 crore people had moved out of poverty during these 12 years. World Bank's latest Poverty and Equity brief, released last week, said that poverty rate in India, defined at $4.2 a day, will decline to 12.1% in 2028.

Article Title: Nita Ambani marks birthday with foundation stone ceremony for 5,000-person care facility
Article Text: Nita Ambani marked her birthday on Sunday by laying the foundation stone for a proposed 100-acre care township in Karjat, Maharashtra. The project, Nita Mukesh Ambani Anant Ashray, is envisioned as a lifelong home for more than 5,000 people, including orphaned children, senior citizens and people with developmental disabilities.Mukesh Ambani and members of the Ambani family attended the bhumi pujan and groundbreaking ceremony near Mumbai. The township, being established by Reliance Foundation, will be developed as a permanent, not-for-profit institution in phases. It is planned as a community with residential homes, healthcare facilities, schools, rehabilitation services and opportunities for education, work and recreation.Nita Ambani said the project was a step towards creating “a loving home for people with disabilities, children who need a home and seniors who seek care and comfort”. She said the township would combine medical support with the warmth of family life and give residents opportunities to learn, work, make friends and participate in festivals and celebrations.According to the plans shared by Reliance Foundation, the township will support a wider community of approximately 15,000 people, including residents, caregivers, medical professionals, support staff and their families.The proposed facility will comprise eight residential villages, each named after a sacred river of India. Residents will live in small, family-style homes supported by house parents and caregivers. Their rooms will be designed to offer familiarity and personal belonging, with residents encouraged to personalise their living spaces.The project will include a specialised hospital offering developmental medicine, epilepsy care, special-needs dentistry, palliative care and other medical services. Rehabilitation facilities for physiotherapy, occupational therapy, speech therapy and hydrotherapy are also planned.Other proposed amenities include a temple, gardens, farms, playgrounds, workshops, cafés and inclusive sports and recreational facilities. An animal companionship farm is expected to be developed with expertise from Vantara.The township will also offer vocational training and employment opportunities through facilities such as a bakery, café and craft studios. A dedicated training academy for disability-care professionals, a hospice wing and a garden of remembrance are also part of the plans.The initiative is expected to have an impact beyond the township. Around 1,000 people from nearby areas are expected to access therapy, education and employment opportunities, while respite-care facilities, mobile medical clinics and outreach programmes will support families in neighbouring districts.
Article Summary: Mukesh Ambani and members of the Ambani family attended the bhumi pujan and groundbreaking ceremony near Mumbai. The township will be developed as a permanent, not-for-profit institution in phases. It is planned as a community with residential homes, healthcare facilities, schools, rehabilitation services and opportunities for education, work and recreation.

Article Title: Three held over pro-Khalistan graffiti at Delhi Metro stations after Diljit concert
Article Text:
The arrests come days after singer Diljit Dosanjh performed in New Delhi.

NEW DELHI: Three people, including a woman, have been arrested for allegedly writing pro-Khalistan slogans at two Delhi Metro stations, police said on Sunday. The graffiti also carried a message targeting singer Diljit Dosanjh.The arrests come days after Dosanjh performed in the national capital on Friday as part of his Aura India Tour. The singer is scheduled to take the tour to several other cities over the next two months.The graffiti was found at Jahangirpuri and Shastri Nagar Metro stations on October 29 and 30, respectively. Police said the accused were allegedly promised substantial financial rewards for defacing public property at prominent locations in Delhi.The arrested persons have been identified as Sumeet alias Raftar (30), a resident of Panipat in Haryana, and Sumit Kumar alias Kaka (22) and Gurpreet (22), both from Punjab.According to Deputy Commissioner of Police (Special Cell) Narra Chaitanya, the investigation revealed that Sumit Kumar was allegedly the main instigator.Sumeet allegedly painted the slogans near Gate No. 1 of Jahangirpuri Metro station and recorded a video of the act to send to his handlers.Kumar and Gurpreet allegedly defaced a staircase wall near Gate No. 2 of Shastri Nagar Metro station."In both instances, the graffiti read "Diljit Singh quam d gaddar khoon d badla SFJ Khalistan", expressing support for the banned separatist organisation Sikhs For Justice (SFJ) and Khalistan ideology. These acts defaced public property in Metro stations and posed a threat to public order and national integrity," the police said, ANI reported.Police said Sumit Kumar had been in contact with SFJ sympathisers in Ludhiana and Gurdaspur before an associate allegedly instructed him to download an encrypted messaging application.A member linked to the banned separatist organisation Sikhs For Justice (SFJ) allegedly shared graffiti templates through the app and offered him financial rewards for carrying out the activity at prominent Metro stations.Kumar then allegedly recruited Gurpreet and Sumeet to execute the plan. The three travelled to Delhi on October 28, police said.Police said Sumeet ad come in contact with Kumar through online platforms and had visited Ludhiana about a week before the incident. The trio travelled to Delhi by taxi and reached ISBT Kashmere Gate on October 29.Investigators also found that Kumar and Gurpreet had known each other for around four years. Kumar allegedly persuaded her to travel to Delhi on the pretext of shopping before informing her about the plan, police said.Police further alleged that Kumar had painted graffiti near the GTK Bypass, under the jurisdiction of Samaypur Badli police station, on October 30. That incident is being investigated separately.Two FIRs were registered at the Metro Azadpur and Metro NSP police stations under Section 3 of the Delhi Prevention of Defacement of Public Property Act, 2007, and Section 62(2) of the Metro Railway (Operation and Maintenance) Act, 2002."Further investigation is underway to identify other persons involved in the network and establish the role of the handlers behind the alleged operation," the officer said.
Article Summary: The arrests come days after singer Diljit Dosanjh performed in New Delhi. The graffiti was found at Jahangirpuri and Shastri Nagar Metro stations. Police said the accused were allegedly promised substantial financial rewards for defacing public property.

Article Title: CBI extradites Mahadev App kingpin Sourabh Chandrakar from Oman
Article Text:
CBI has extradited Sourabh Chandrakar from Oman

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: In a major breakthrough against transnational organized crime, CBI in coordination with other Central agencies, has extradited Sourabh Chandrakar, the promoter and alleged kingpin of the Mahadev App illegal online betting syndicate, from the Sultanate of Oman.A special CBI team travelled to Muscat, took custody of Chandrakar, and escorted him back to India. Following a mandatory medical examination and the acquisition of a transit remand, he will be taken to Raipur and produced before the CBI Special Judge Monday.Chandrakar is wanted in two CBI cases, in which chargesheets have already been filed, as well as an Enforcement Directorate (ED) case where a prosecution complaint has been submitted and several properties in India and abroad have been attached.The investigation into the Mahadev Online Book cases was taken up by the CBI at the request of the Chhattisgarh government.The probe revealed that the syndicate operated as one of the country's largest illegal online betting networks run from outside India, facilitating unlawful betting on cricket, football, card games, and other events through a widespread system of franchised "panels" and "branches."Proceeds from the illegal betting network were funneled through numerous mule bank accounts, layered via multiple transactions, and moved overseas through hawala channels.CBI investigations also established that a portion of the illicit funds was used to pay protection money to public servants to ensure the unhindered operation of the syndicate.Chargesheets in the matter have been filed under the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988, provisions of the Indian Penal Code relating to criminal conspiracy, cheating, and forgery, as well as the Chhattisgarh Gambling (Prohibition) Act, with Chandrakar named as a key accused.Chandrakar was initially located and detained by the Royal Oman Police following a Red Corner Notice issued against him. Subsequent extradition proposals, accompanied by gathered evidence, were submitted by the CBI and ED, and pursued in close coordination with Indian government agencies, the Interpol National Central Bureau, and Omani authorities.The CBI expressed gratitude to the Government of the Sultanate of Oman and the Royal Oman Police for their cooperation, highlighting the strong bilateral relations and mutual commitment to combating international crime. The extradition represents a key milestone in India's ongoing efforts to hold foreign-based fugitives accountable under Indian law, CBI said.
Article Summary: Sourabh Chandrakar is the promoter and alleged kingpin of the Mahadev App illegal online betting syndicate. He is wanted in two CBI cases, in which chargesheets have already been filed. Chandrakar will be taken to Raipur and produced before the CBI Special Judge Monday.

Article Title: 'Rahul trying to sideline Priyanka': BJP's big attack after INDIA bloc's Ramlila Maidan rally

NEW DELHI: BJP on Sunday accused Congress leader Rahul Gandhi of attempting to sideline his sister Priyanka Gandhi Vadra, alleging that she was deliberately denied an opportunity to speak at the INDIA bloc rally at Delhi's Ramlila Maidan.BJP national spokesperson Pradeep Bhandari claimed that the developments reflected growing divisions within the Congress, with the Rahul Gandhi and Priyanka Gandhi camps competing for influence within the party."Priyanka Vadra, who has served as the General Secretary of the Congress Party and is Rahul Gandhi’s sister, was not allowed to speak today at the Ramlila Ground. Did Rahul Gandhi prevent her from speaking today?" Bhandari said.He further alleged that Priyanka was kept in the background during Saturday's mock parliament exercise, which he described as Rahul Gandhi's relaunch exercise."And not just today, even yesterday during the Mock Parliament, when Rahul Gandhi's relaunch exercise was taking place, Priyanka Vadra's chair was placed in the second row, and she was not allowed to speak there either," he said."The Rahul camp is insecure about the Priyanka camp, and the Priyanka camp is being suppressed," Bhandari alleged, claiming that Rahul Gandhi was more concerned about sidelining his sister than addressing issues concerning the country or the Congress."Rahul Gandhi, who is undergoing his hundredth relaunch, is not talking about the people of the country or about the Congress Party today; instead, he is merely trying to sideline Priyanka Gandhi Vadra," he added."Between Rahul versus Priyanka, the Congress is divided into two factions, and the public is watching this fight while eating popcorn," the BJP spokesperson said.The BJP's attack came as Rahul Gandhi led the INDIA bloc's rally against alleged electoral irregularities and the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls. Addressing supporters, the Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha launched a sharp attack on the Election Commission, Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Union home minister Amit Shah over allegations of 'vote chori'.Gandhi warned that Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar would be removed from his post and face imprisonment, while asserting that Modi and Shah would also face legal action over the alleged electoral irregularities."After Gyanesh Kumar, we will stand against you," Gandhi said, warning the BJP leadership not to think it could escape accountability.The rally was attended by several INDIA bloc leaders, including Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge, Sonia Gandhi, Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav and TMC chief Mamata Banerjee, among others.
Article Summary: BJP national spokesperson Pradeep Bhandari claimed that the developments reflected growing divisions within the Congress. The Rahul Gandhi and Priyanka Gandhi camps competing for influence within the party, he said. The attack came as Rahul Gandhi led the INDIA bloc's rally against alleged electoral irregularities and the Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls.

Article Title: Bhutan dedicates Buddhist stupa to PM Modi; Rijiju calls it ‘huge honour’ for India
Article Text:
Union minister Kiren Rijiju during a meeting with Bhutan's King Jigme Khesar Namgyel Wangchuck during his visit to Gelephu, Bhutan (PTI)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Bhutan's King Jigme Khesar Namgyel Wangchuck has dedicated a sacred Buddhist stupa to Prime Minister Narendra Modi, recognising his contribution to strengthening friendship between the two countries. The dedication of Stupa number 76 took place during a ceremony to raise and consecrate 108 stupas in Gelephu Mindfulness City on Sunday.According to news agency ANI, Union minority affairs minister Kiren Rijiju represented India at the ceremony and expressed gratitude to Bhutan for the gesture, describing it as a "huge honour for India". He also conveyed gratitude on behalf of Prime Minister Modi to the Bhutanese King.In a post on X, Rijiju said, "It's a huge honour for India that very sacred stupa 76 is dedicated to Hon'ble PM Narendra Modi ji for his outstanding vision and commitment to friendship between India and Bhutan. On the auspicious occasion of Lhabab Duchen, joined the sacred ceremony in Gelephu Mindfulness City, Bhutan, marking the raising and consecration of 108 stupas, accompanied by the blowing of Dungchens."He further said, "Paid my respects and offered prayers in the presence of His Majesty the King of Bhutan, Her Majesty the Gyaltsuen, H E Dasho Tshering Tobgay, Prime Minister of Bhutan & the people of Bhutan.A deeply meaningful spiritual occasion, reflecting Bhutan’s rich Buddhist heritage and the enduring bonds of friendship between our two nations."Stupas are sacred Buddhist structures associated with the teachings and life of Gautama Buddha. Traditionally, they were built to preserve the relics of the Buddha and other revered Buddhist figures, including their ashes and remains. Over time, they became important places of worship, meditation and religious devotion.The 108 stupas in Bhutan are known as Jangchub Chortens, or Stupas of Enlightenment. The number 108 holds special significance in Buddhist traditions and is associated with religious practices, including the use of 108 beads in prayer malas. The structures are intended to promote peace, harmony and spiritual well-being.Rijiju is visiting Bhutan from October 31 to November 2. Earlier on Sunday, Rijiju met Bhutanese Prime Minister Tshering Tobgay in Gelephu. The two leaders discussed strengthening the India-Bhutan partnership and exploring the potential of the Gelephu Mindfulness City project.
Article Summary: Bhutan's King Jigme Khesar Namgyel Wangchuck has dedicated a sacred Buddhist stupa to Prime Minister Narendra Modi. The dedication of Stupa number 76 took place during a ceremony to raise and consecrate 108 stupas in Gelephu Mindfulness City. Union minority affairs minister Kiren Rijiju represented India at the ceremony and expressed gratitude to Bhutan for the gesture.

NEW DELHI: Andhra Pradesh Congress president YS Sharmila has shifted her daughter's wedding to another venue after her brother, YS Jagan Mohan Reddy , refused to allow his Bengaluru property to be used for the ceremony.In a social media post on X, Sharmila defended her ownership claim over the Yelahanka property and said it was allotted entirely to her and her children as part of the division of family assets after her brother Jagan Reddy became chief minister.“What is mine is mine, but the greed to covet it is not in my nature. This is the truth, with God as my witness," Sharmila said."Since it is my children's right and the house where my father YSR lived, we wanted to hold my daughter Anjili's wedding there, as she had wished. Ask any household in Telugu society, and they will tell you that getting one's daughter married in one's own house is considered a blessing for every parent," she added.Sharmila said she had decided to organise her daughter's wedding ceremony elsewhere as it was her responsibility to ensure that the event remained free of controversy."However, we are very saddened that we could not fulfil my daughter's wish to have her wedding at the very house where she grew up. My salutations to everyone who felt concerned about my daughter after seeing the developments taking place over the wedding venue," she said."My daughter Anjili's marriage is a match arranged by elders. It is our responsibility to conduct the wedding without controversy and without any disputes. Therefore, we have decided to hold the wedding ceremony of YS Anjili Reddy and Somala Raghuram Reddy at a different venue instead of the Yelahanka house, in the presence of relatives, friends and well-wishers. We wholeheartedly wish that the Telugu people will shower their blessings and good wishes on the couple,” she added.This comes after Jagan Mohan Reddy cited security reasons for refusing to let out the Yelahanka Palace for the wedding ceremony of his niece, Anjili Reddy, in Bengaluru.In the letter, he pointed out that a wedding would bring a large number of guests, caterers, decorators, photographers and other service providers into the residential premises."At the end of the day, this is my home and I want to ensure that my family and I are safe here," Jagan wrote.
Article Summary: Andhra Pradesh Congress president YS Sharmila has shifted her daughter's wedding to another venue. Her brother, YS Jagan Mohan Reddy, refused to allow his Bengaluru property to be used for the ceremony. Jagan cited security reasons for refusing to let out the Yelahanka Palace for the wedding ceremony.

NEW DELHI: Around 2.5 lakh shops across 20 to 25 major markets in Delhi remained closed on Sunday, with traders claiming losses of Rs 10,000-11,000 crore due to disruptions caused by the INDIA bloc rally at Ramlila Maidan during the peak Diwali shopping season.Chamber of Trade & Industry (CTI) chairman Brijesh Goyal said nearly 80% of the approximately three lakh shops in markets surrounding the rally venue remained shut amid concerns over traffic restrictions, congestion and the expected arrival of large crowds.The disruption also affected the movement of customers, suppliers and dealers from towns surrounding the national capital. According to Goyal, around three lakh to four lakh people who regularly travel to Delhi for business did not arrive, while approximately 5,000 vehicles, including tempos and trucks, could not transport goods to markets in Old Delhi and Central Delhi.“Due to the rally held at Ramlila Maidan today, about 20 to 25 major markets in the vicinity were affected. These historic markets house approximately 3,00,000 shops. Based on data we received this evening from various WhatsApp groups—comprising traders from different markets under the CTA (Confederation of All India Traders)—about 80% of these shops—roughly 2,50,000 out of 3,00,000—remained closed today,” he said.Goyal added that loading and unloading operations were disrupted, affecting wholesale and retail businesses during one of the busiest periods of the year.“The movement of goods—loading and unloading—was completely disrupted. During the peak Diwali season, these markets with individual turnovers collectively generate business worth approximately 10,000 to 12,000 crore rupees. Even where shops remained open, sales were virtually non-existent; there were simply no customers,” he said.Putting the estimated losses at Rs 10,000-11,000 crore, Goyal questioned who would compensate traders for the business disruption.“The question now arises: who will compensate for this loss, or who will make up for it—will the organisers do so?” he said.He said the timing of the rally had compounded the impact, as traders were preparing for the festive rush ahead of Dhanteras, scheduled four days later. Businesses in the affected markets depend heavily on the movement of customers and goods during this period.Ahead of the gathering, traders across several major commercial hubs in Delhi had opposed holding the rally at Ramlila Maidan during the peak Diwali shopping season. They warned that traffic congestion and restrictions could disrupt wholesale markets and affect the livelihoods of thousands of daily-wage workers.The Automotive Parts Merchant Association (APMA), based at Kashmere Gate, said the rally's location could affect commercial activity across a three-kilometre radius, covering several major trading hubs in the capital.APMA president Vinay Narang said traders were not opposed to democratic protests but objected to the timing and choice of venue."We are not aligned with any political party, nor are we against democratic protests. But the timing and the venue are completely wrong. Ramlila Maidan is located in the middle of Asia’s largest commercial zone—with major markets like Chandni Chowk, Sadar Bazaar, Daryaganj, Mori Gate, and Kashmere Gate within a three-kilometre radius," Narang said.Amid concerns raised by traders' associations, Congress leader Rahul Gandhi had appealed to people travelling to Delhi for the rally to support local businesses by shopping from their stores during the festive season.In a video message posted on X on Saturday, Gandhi urged participants to combine their participation in the protest with shopping from small businesses.“Tomorrow, lakhs of people are coming to Delhi for the Ramlila March. It is the festive season. The time of Diwali, Chhath, and Bhai Dooj has arrived. I want those lakhs of people coming to Delhi from outside to support the traders here,” Gandhi said.“Protest, march, hold rallies, and along with that, do a little shopping too - it will benefit the traders,” he added.The leader of opposition in the Lok Sabha also accused the BJP of spreading rumours about the rally's potential economic impact.“I know the rally will not harm the traders. The BJP is scared, that's why it's spreading rumours,” he said, adding, “But let's do both. Tomorrow there will be a march, there will be a rally, and lakhs of people will buy goods from the small shops of our traders.”The INDIA bloc held the rally at Ramlila Maidan on Sunday to protest against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, alleging irregularities in the exercise.Several Opposition leaders attended the gathering, including Lok Sabha leader of opposition Rahul Gandhi, Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge, former West Bengal chief minister Mamata Banerjee and Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav. Protesters also raised slogans such as "Vote chor, gaddi chhod", demanding accountability over alleged electoral irregularities.
Article Summary: Around 2.5 lakh shops across 20 to 25 major markets in Delhi remained closed on Sunday. Traders claim losses of Rs 10,000-11,000 crore due to disruptions caused by the INDIA bloc rally at Ramlila Maidan during the peak Diwali shopping season.

NEW DELHI: Paving the way for final production of the country’s first indigenous Bullet Train, B28, the “Squeeze Test” or vehicle body shell test of the first coach is underway and will be completed next week. Railway minister Ashwini Vaishnaw witnessed the test at BEML’s Bengaluru facility on Sunday.A squeeze test is a safety assessment to determine whether a train’s car body can withstand heavy external forces and pressure without excessive deformation or structural failure in case of a collision or crash. “Squeeze test of the integrated car body is at final stage. After this, propulsion system will be placed and all electronic systems will be put in place. Subsequently, a climatic test will be carried out wherein the car will be subjected to tests at high temperature of 50 degree Celsius and negative temperature, and dusty and heavy rain environment conditions,” Vaishnaw said.Railways plans to start the test run of the high-speed train, designed to operate at a maximum speed of 249 kmph and a testing speed of 275 kmph, from first quarter of 2027-2028 on Surat-Vapi (100 km) section of Ahmedabad-Mumbai High Speed corridor.The commercial run is scheduled for August 2027. Each bullet train will have eight coaches and another eight can be added later. The eight-car train can carry 557 passengers.BEML, a central PSU, is manufacturing the first two of the indigenous bullet trains, each comprising eight coaches.“After the successful completion of this test, the prototype should ideally be ready in less than six months. Since the B28 (Bharat 28) train is not being built on Japanese Shinkansen technology, the development process should not take much time. The squeeze test establishes whether the body retains its shape under pressure and whether the passenger compartment maintains its structural integrity,” an official said.While seeking Cabinet approval for the escalated cost of the country’s first bullet train project, the railway ministry had stated that two prototype trains were expected to be ready for trial runs in the first quarter of 2027. It had also said that the entire Gujarat section of the corridor was expected to be completed by December 2027, while the full 508-km Mumbai-Ahmedabad High Speed Rail corridor is targeted for completion by December 2030.
Article Summary: The squeeze test is a safety assessment to determine whether a train’s car body can withstand heavy external forces and pressure without excessive deformation or structural failure. Railway minister Ashwini Vaishnaw witnessed the test at BEML's Bengaluru facility on Sunday.
