Six Indian trekkers, including four men and two women, remained stranded in Nepal's snowbound Upper Dolpa region Sunday after allegedly ignoring weather warnings and leaving their guide behind to continue towards Shey-Phoksundo Lake. A technical fault in a Nepal Army helicopter delayed rescue efforts, while heavy snowfall linked to Cyclone Arnab made mountain trails inaccessible.The six - Moumita Halder, Piyali Koley, Jajla Trivedi Kumar, Aditya Singha, Diplina Biswas and Rajesh De - got stranded on Saturday afternoon in Danigad, roughly 300km northwest of Kathmandu. Their destination, Shey-Phoksundo Lake, lies at an altitude of about 3,600 metres and is considered Nepal's deepest lake, with an estimated depth of 145 metres.Nepal's Department of Hydrology and Meteorology had warned of rain, heavy snow and avalanche risks between Oct 29 and 31, prompting restrictions on high-altitude travel. Dolpa chief district officer Junu Hamal Dhakal said, "The group continued towards the lake despite warnings from security personnel and their Nepalese guide about worsening weather. They left the guide behind and pressed ahead as snowfall intensified, disregarding restrictions the district administration had imposed on travel towards Upper Dolpa.Locals also warned them that heavy snow could make the mountain passes impassable."The guide alerted authorities on Saturday evening after losing contact with the trekkers. By Sunday morning, the administration had mobilised security personnel and sought helicopter assistance. "We have located the area where they are stranded, and an Army helicopter is arriving to rescue them. We hope to rescue them soon," Dhakal said.However, the helicopter stationed at Surkhet air base could not take off because of a technical fault, forcing authorities to arrange another aircraft. "Rescue initiatives are continuing with the use of a Nepal Army helicopter. However, telephone contact is not viable with the tourists as there is no mobile network in the area where they are stranded," Dhakal said.

Article Title: SC upholds HC order allowing I-T to reassess income of ex-CJI's sons
Article Text:
SC allows tax department to reopen assessment of former CJI YK Sabharwal's sons over Rs 255 crore share sale deals.

2015 notice of assessing officer issued on reasons duly recorded and is valid: SC

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Holding that the income tax department is not precluded from conducting reassessment upon discovering evidence suggesting income had escaped assessment, Supreme Court upheld a Delhi high court order allowing the agency to reassess the income of the sons of former Chief Justice of India YK Sabharwal for 2008-09 and 2009-10.A bench of Justices J B Pardiwala and K Vinod Chandran dismissed the Sabharwals' appeal and said the notice issued by the department in 2015 was valid as it was based on reasons duly recorded and on tangible material of a report of its investigation unit.Recording details of financial transactions, the Supreme Court bench noted Chetan Sabharwal along with his brother Nitin Sabharwal and two other shareholders entered into two share purchase agreements with GYS Real Estate Pvt Ltd (buyer company) for a sale of 7.5 lakh equity shares of Pawan Impex (P) Ltd and 2.5 lakh equity shares of SVIIT Software (P) Ltd held by each of the parties for a sale consideration of Rs 195 crore and Rs 60 crore, respectively. The appellant and other selling shareholders were each entitled to 1/4th share of the total consideration. "We are of the firm view that the impugned notice dated March 31, 2015, issued by the assessing officer under Section 148 of Income Tax Act, for initiating reassessment for assessment years 2008-09 and 2009-10, was issued on reasons duly recorded and is valid," the bench said."The reasons rest on tangible material, namely the report of the DGIT Investigation Unit, Noida, which concluded that shares of company No.1 (Pawan Impex (P) Ltd) and company No. 2 (SVIIT Software (P) Ltd) were overvalued when compared with the cost of their land and building, and they have a rational nexus and a live link with the belief formed by the assessing officer," it said.Subsequent to completion of assessment, the investigation unit conducted enquiries into the value of the shares of Pawan Impex (P) Ltd and SVIIT Software (P) Ltd and prepared a report. The report concluded, prima facie, that the shares were overvalued when compared with the cost of their land and building, which was much lower than the transaction amounts of Rs 195 crore and Rs 60 crore, respectively.The enquiries revealed the appellants purchased one-half share of the property at Sikandara Road, Delhi, in April 2010 through a court auction, and that the major source of this investment was the sale proceeds of the shares of the companies. On perusal of the investigation report and after a gap of four years, the department issued a notice under Section 148 of the act for reassessment.
Article Summary: Supreme Court upheld a Delhi high court order allowing the agency to reassess the income of the sons of former Chief Justice of India YK Sabharwal for 2008-09 and 2009-10. A bench of Justices J B Pardiwala and K Vinod Chandran dismissed the Sabharwals' appeal.

New Delhi: Public sector Coal India Limited (CIL) recorded its highest-ever monthly supplies at 70.3 million tonnes (MT), registering a robust 19% growth over the 59.2 MT supplied during the corresponding period in FY26, despite operational challenges posed by unseasonal rainfall, Puja festivities and the impact of a cyclone, amid rising power demand.The previous monthly record of 69.4 MT was achieved in March 2026, CIL said in a statement. Article Title: International Digi Yatra trials to begin at 7 airports for Indian nationals this year for wider rollout in 2027: Government

NEW DELHI: Travelling abroad from India could soon be a seamless experience just like taking domestic flights with Digi Yatra (DY). India will hold trials for international passengers at seven airports in the three months of this year, allowing eligible Indian nationals holding e-passports to use DY at designated airport touchpoints while travelling on select flights operated by Air India and IndiGo.The aviation ministry said trials are being conducted at Delhi, Bengaluru, Hyderabad, Cochin, Mumbai, Chennai and Amritsar airports. “Eligible passengers will be able to use the facility at terminal entry points, security hold areas (SHA) and boarding gates, wherever the required infrastructure is available. Feedback received during the trial period will inform the planning of a wider rollout in 2027,” it said in a statement.To access this facility, eligible Indian nationals will need to create an e-passport-based “verifiable credential” (VC) through DY mobile application. “The process involves scanning the machine readable zone (MRZ) of e-passport, reading the embedded chip using the near field communication (NFC) feature of a compatible smartphone, capturing a selfie and verifying the details. The credential is stored in the passenger’s Digi Yatra wallet on the device and can be used at airport touchpoints enabled for the trials,” the statement said.The facility will complement, and not replace, existing travel processes. “Passengers must continue to carry their travel documents and complete all mandatory airline document checks, immigration procedures and other applicable travel formalities,” it added.IndiGo said eligible passengers can upload their boarding pass to the Digi Yatra app. After completing mandatory document verification at airline check-in counter, they can proceed through the security hold area and boarding gates using DY biometric face authentication.IndiGo chief digital and information officer Neetan Chopra said: “At IndiGo, we are committed to redefining air travel by making it more seamless, efficient, and customer centric, and we believe that technology can be a key catalyst in this evolution. Having been a key part of the technical proof of concept earlier this year, we are pleased to partner with Digi Yatra for the launch of these international passenger trials. Article Summary: India will trial Digi Yatra for international passengers at seven airports over the next three months. To access this facility, eligible Indian nationals will need to create an e-passport-based “verifiable credential” (VC) through DY mobile application.
